runs.why: setup shell scripts + requirements split — the #164 anchor
runs.summary: Adds one-command setup scripts for macOS and Windows plus reorganized dependency files. Scripts are reasonable but have a couple of fragile assumptions worth flagging: hardcoded paths and silent failures on password-protected Postgres installs on Windows, and reliance on Homebrew's default Apple Silicon path on macOS.

comments.comment: PATH is hardcoded to /opt/homebrew (Apple Silicon default); on Intel Macs Homebrew installs under /usr/local, so this will silently fail to put pg tools on PATH.

psql -U postgres will fail/hang if a password was set during PostgreSQL install (no PGPASSWORD or -w flag), since psql will prompt interactively and the script has no handling for auth failure. This can cause the script to hang waiting for input instead of failing cleanly.
comments.suggestion: Set PGPASSWORD or add -w with clear error handling, and detect auth failure explicitly rather than relying on findstr on the CREATE DATABASE output.

The implementation correctly separates the metric's two failure modes (never fail a review over a bad timestamp; never silently misattribute an offset as latency) and validates aware-vs-naive datetimes at the right boundaries. I don't see any correctness, security, or architectural issues in the diff worth blocking on.

Well-structured PR implementing route protection and a user menu, with thorough test coverage. No substantive issues found in the diff; the guard logic, return-to stash/clear semantics, and accessibility choices are well reasoned and consistent.
